### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 561d532c4ab723ee9abb69d2b2018cbe39f7171b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `93b3356273bb84d1ec0d7126459c7efe7a7d0406` — the merge of head `8f94aaf619f381a499d8755bea6abd821f682a62` into base `561d532c4ab723ee9abb69d2b2018cbe39f7171b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 93b3356273bb84d1ec0d7126459c7efe7a7d0406 && git checkout 93b3356273bb84d1ec0d7126459c7efe7a7d0406
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 561d532c4ab723ee9abb69d2b2018cbe39f7171b 8f94aaf619f381a499d8755bea6abd821f682a62 && git checkout -B drift-repro 561d532c4ab723ee9abb69d2b2018cbe39f7171b && git merge --no-ff 8f94aaf619f381a499d8755bea6abd821f682a62

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 561d532c4ab723ee9abb69d2b2018cbe39f7171b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 561d532c4ab723ee9abb69d2b2018cbe39f7171b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8f94aaf619f381a499d8755bea6abd821f682a62`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`actionHandlerOwnerRefusal`, `collectHandlerOwnerCandidates`, `reachedHandlerEntry`, `dispatchesThroughHandlerRegistry`, the `invokeBusinessAction` call site), packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts (the `handleActionsRequest` call site), packages/runtime/src/domains/action-handler-owner-gates.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-disabled-package.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`actionPermissionError`, `disabledActionRefusal`, `executeRegisteredAction`, `registeredActionHandlerProbe`, `resolveRouteActionDeclaration`, `collectActionDeclarations`, `resolveActionByName`), packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts (`resolveActionHandlerKeys`, `actionHandlerObjectKeys`, `standaloneActionOwnerKey`, `isObjectLessActionKey`), packages/objectql/src/engine-actions.ts (`registerAction`, `registerActionOverride`, `executeAction`, `listRegisteredActions`, `removeActionsByPackage`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (`resyncAuthoredActionsNow`, `readAuthoredActionRows`, `runGovernanceInventory`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`listItems`), packages/objectql/src/engine-object-repository.ts (`execute`), packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts (action-body binding), packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts (`installDefaultActionBodyRunner`), packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts (`listActions`, `readMergedItems`, the `run_action` wiring), packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts (the three `/actions` mounts), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`handleActions`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts and protocol-meta-list-reads.ts (`getMetaItems`), packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts and data-action-routes.ts (read to exclude them), packages/services/service-automation/src (read to exclude it). Prose faces (.changeset/action-handler-owner-gates.md, content/docs/ui/actions.mdx) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; both were read sentence by sentence here because the module header and the doc bullet carry the same rule.

Face: the file list decides no face (no published schema, no governed path; `@objectstack/runtime` is a published package and `check:api-surface` is spec-only — the two new exports `actionHandlerOwnerRefusal` and `ActionHandlerOwnerRefusal` are additive and reach the runtime entry through `action-execution.ts`, a widening of the package's own surface, not of a published schema). The committed changeset's line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the closed-pair spelling AGENTS.md step 3 names, so the face is narrowing and the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` with ④. Rule under review: a `script` action whose dispatch reaches a handler entry that a different declared action's own dispatch reaches answers with that owner's `requiredPermissions` (403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`) and its activation switch (409 `ACTION_DISABLED`) as a union with its own, at both action doors; a borrowed entry built from a metadata-plane declaration is refused 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` while the plane cannot be read. Full review (no prior at-tier record on any head; the PR thread carries only the docs-drift bot; no `Contract-review-claim:` or hold line).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set narrowed, correctly stated.** Both doors call one function, `actionHandlerOwnerRefusal`, immediately after their own ADR-0066 D4 gate and ADR-0126 activation consult and ahead of the ADR-0104 param contract, the confirmation gate, the subject-record load and the invocation row (`actions.ts` lines 679-698; `action-execution.ts` lines 4347-4355). The REST door maps the refusal onto its envelope with `code`; the MCP door throws it with `code` and `status`, the shape `resolveThrownHttpError` reads. Only `script` declarations that are not the declarative update are judged (`dispatchesThroughHandlerRegistry`), which is exactly the population `executeRegisteredAction` dispatches; `flow`, `api` and declarative-update actions reach no registry entry and are rightly outside. Correct.
2. **Entry and rotation.** The entry judged is the first `object:key` of `actionHandlerObjectKeys(objectName)` × the door's own candidate list that one `listRegisteredActions()` snapshot holds — the same walk `executeRegisteredAction` performs and `registeredActionHandlerProbe` already mirrors. REST hands the gate `resolveActionHandlerKeys(actionDef, actionName)` and dispatches with the same call (`actions.ts` line 1077); MCP hands `resolveActionHandlerKeys(action)` and dispatches with the same (`action-execution.ts` line 4633). The legacy `*` key sits last in both walks and is object-less for the population read. Correct: the entry the gate judges is the entry the dispatch reaches.
3. **Owner identity.** Identity = (owning object key, name). The invoked declaration's key is the routed object when the routed object embeds that name (both doors resolve object-embedded first, and `collectActionDeclarations` makes the embedded copy win on a key clash), else `standaloneActionOwnerKey(action)` — the same ladder the resync registers under. A declaration carried twice (embedded and as a standalone item) therefore has one identity and is skipped as the invoked one; two objects declaring one name are two identities and are coupled only when their dispatches reach one entry. Both pinned ("one declaration carried object-embedded and as a standalone copy", "a same-named action on another object"). Correct.
4. **Population scoping per entry.** For an entry under a real object key only declarations whose rotation starts at that key can reach it — the routed object's embedded `actions[]` and standalone items owned by that object — and that is what is read (the door's resolved object, the engine's schema, every standalone source). For an object-less entry (`global`, `*`) any object's embedded declaration can reach it, so every object is read (engine registry and the plane's merged object listing). Sources are unioned (engine copies: `registry.getAllObjects`, `registry.listItems('action', …, { includeDisabledPackages: true })`; plane: the protocol's served `getMetaItems`, else the metadata service's `listObjects` / `loadMany`), so a disabled package's declaration still gates its handler, and a served override's row and its base's row both count (every copy under one identity is judged for permissions). More rows can only add gates. Correct, and complete against the three rungs `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` resolves through.
5. **Gate order.** Owner permissions for every copy of every owner first, then owner switches — the doors' own order, so the switch is no oracle to a caller the owner would refuse. `disabledActionRefusal` is keyed by the declarative name, as the ledger is. Correct.
6. **Every door that dispatches to registered handlers, enumerated independently.** Two callers of `executeRegisteredAction` exist in the tree (REST `handleActionsRequest`, reached from the three `dispatcher-plugin.ts` mounts including the object-less `//:action` form and from `HttpDispatcher.handleActions`; MCP `invokeBusinessAction`, reached from `run_action`), and both pass the gate. One other caller of `ql.executeAction` exists: `ObjectRepository.execute` (`engine-object-repository.ts` line 141), the in-process `ctx.api.object(x).execute(...)` a body or hook reaches; it carries no declaration and no caller identity, runs elevated by construction, and is recorded as outside the consult points by `disabledActionRefusal`'s own header — what bounds it is the doors above it and who may author a body, not this rule; legitimately outside. Not doors: MCP `list_actions` (advertises through `registeredActionHandlerProbe`, dispatches nothing), the REST batch routes and data-action routes (data verbs only), the automation engine (no node dispatches to the action registry; a `flow`-type action dispatches a flow), the declared-endpoint seam (`api` type forwards in-process), `resume_run` (no registry dispatch), the Console's `ActionEngine` (a client that calls the REST door; its button-side `requiredPermissions` read is the acceptance note's unchanged surface, and the server remains the source of truth). The sandbox `body-runner` manufactures handlers and dispatches none. Covered: every door.
7. **Snapshot and dispatch.** The registry snapshot is taken in the gate; the dispatch reads the live map after the param contract, the confirmation gate and the subject-record load. The map moves only on a package bind/unbind or an authored-action resync, so the window is the request's own awaits and is crossed only by a metadata-plane write landing inside it — a write whose author already holds a stronger capability than the window grants. Not a finding at this tier; the module header does not record the window (should, ④).
8. **Fail-closed behaviour.** An engine that cannot enumerate its handlers answers `undefined` (the probe and the activation consult take the same stance on such an engine; the production engine always enumerates). A throwing engine copy or a failing `resolveService` propagates to the door's catch. A throwing plane listing is reported, never read as empty, and refuses 503 exactly the entry whose owner's gates live only on the plane (package `metadata-service`, entry ≠ invoked identity); an action's own plane-built handler and a package-registered handler keep running on the engine's copies. Pinned (three legs). Correct, and the one fail-open-looking arm (plane-only owner of a package-registered handler during an outage) is the one the changeset states.
9. **Legitimate shared-handler patterns.** The repo's shipped code carries no two declarations on one handler key (the body's reading, not re-measured here; the `registerAction` call sites read — plugin-auth's invitation link, the artifact binder, the resync — each bind a declaration's own key); the one fixture that did (`actions-disabled-package.test.ts`) was two gates on one key, which is the shape the rule says to split, and it now pins what it pinned. The doc bullet tells authors to give each action its own key unless both should share one gate. Nothing legitimate breaks.
10. **Envelope and codes.** `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(403)` → `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `ACTION_DISABLED_CODE` reused, `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(503)` → `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; no new code (ADR-0112), no tracker number in any runtime string (`check:doc-authoring`). Every refusal pin asserts `status` and `code` (REST through the envelope, MCP through the thrown error) and that the owner's handler was never called; every allow pin asserts the handler ran exactly once. Correct.
11. **Tests are rule tests.** 17 cases organised per door over the `HttpDispatcher` and `invokeBusinessAction` with a handler registry double that keeps `engine-actions.ts`'s key shape and miss sentence; test names state the rule. The double has no `protocol` service and no `registry.listItems` / `getAllObjects`, so the unit file pins the metadata-service fallback arm of the owner read and not the protocol-listing or registry-listing arms; those arms were verified by reading here (`getMetaItems` answers `{ type, items }` and the reader accepts both that and a bare array, as `mcp.ts`'s `readMergedItems` does; `listItems` takes the `includeDisabledPackages` option; `getAllObjects` is on the engine contract). Should, ④. Premise, ablation (five anchors, each restored blob-equal), the 91/91 targeted run, the 8726-test runtime suite at `9b2ba60b94` and the 3513-test dogfood battery at head are the dev's readings, named to their heads; the code under test is identical between `9b2ba60b94` and head except for the type-only follow-up (`HandlerOwnerListingRead`).
12. **Public surface.** `actionHandlerOwnerRefusal` and `ActionHandlerOwnerRefusal` are new exports of `action-execution.ts`; additive, typed with the package's existing `ActionExecutionDeps` / `HttpProtocolContext`. No published schema moves. `no (narrowing)` is the correct arm.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/action-handler-owner-gates.md`: `@objectstack/runtime: minor`, title with `!`, a BREAKING banner, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), and the author's remedy (one handler key per action). AGENTS.md step 3: the meaning of an authorable value moved — a `target` naming another declaration's handler key now carries that declaration's gates, and nothing an author can write is refused — so `semantic` is the right kind (`narrowed` would need a refused value or a tightened authoring requirement; `none` would understate it); a kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves, so `minor` follows; the `(narrowing)` arm keeps the banner and the disposition marker. `check-changeset-no-major`'s own self-test rows read this exact pairing as `none-clean`. The PR body carries both declaration lines at line start. `Skills-docs: none` is present and its reasoning holds: `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` teaches `target` as a registered handler name and `requiredPermissions` as the action's own gate, and neither sentence turns false. Touched packages: `@objectstack/runtime` (published, changeset present); `content/docs` is not a package. Consistent — confirmed as declared.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); no other login to name. Draft, base `main`, head repo equals base repo, `auto_merge` null, no governed path in the six-file list, 733/1 changed lines. Commit trailers are the model-free pair.
- Closing keywords: none in the body, correct for a security-seat PR with no card.
- Acceptance notes, each answered: (1) the Console button reads only its own action's `requiredPermissions`, so a button whose handler belongs to a gated action can be shown and then refused — accepted; the server is the source of truth (ADR-0066 D4's own sentence), and a listing that admits then refuses is the fail-closed direction; a follow-up for the UI gate is the seat's call. (2) Fixture authors who give two actions one key now get one gate — accepted; the doc bullet states the remedy.
- Residuals the dispatch names (a disabled package's object-less handler under a declaration with no `requiredPermissions`; the owner's `ai.exposed`; MCP `list_actions` listing then `run_action` refusing; the MCP door's own direct D4 throw without `code`/`status`): none is claimed fixed by the PR, none counts here; one further scope limit of the same class is in the reviewer's local note, not here.
- Docs drift bot: four pages named; `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 49 ("Action `requiredPermissions` bypassed … `actionPermissionError`") stays true — the new gate reaches the same stand-down through the same function and adds no second one; the other three are literal `getMetaItems` hits inside the new type alias. No sentence turns false.
- Test budget: the new file boots no kernel; no `test-budget:` line owed.
- CI at head `8f94aaf619` at review time: 23 success, 12 skipped, 4 still running (`Test Core` shards, `Build Core`, a lint lane), 0 failed. A landing still requires every check green on this head (contract-review.md ②); the lane re-reads before enqueueing.

### ④ Design judgment

On the narrowing face, the narrowing is judged against the published contract on `main`. ADR-0110 D2 makes a handler key an addressing fact and not an action's identity, and ADR-0126 §8 item 2 placed the activation consult at the declaration for that reason; `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` already states that a `flow` action inherits its target flow's `requiredPermissions` and that the caller needs both when both declare. The diff extends that reading to the `script` arm — a handler has the gates of every declaration that dispatches to it, unioned — at the two doors where a resolved declaration exists, through one function with the doors' own gate order, and takes nothing away from a declaration with its own handler key. Owner identity is read at the entry the dispatch reaches, in the dispatch's own rotation, from one snapshot, with every source the declaration resolution reads unioned; the plane-outage arm refuses exactly the entry whose owner's gates cannot be read anywhere else and keeps the rest running, which is ADR-0110 D3's posture applied as narrowly as it can be. The envelope reuses two standard codes and the existing `ACTION_DISABLED`. The design holds, and it lands without a protocol change, as the changeset says.

No must-fix.

Not blocking, recorded for the seat and the lane:

- **should** — pin the production arms of the owner read: one case with a `protocol` double answering `{ type, items }` and a `registry` double carrying `listItems` / `getAllObjects`, so the arms the composed runtime takes are held by a test and not by this reading (① item 11).
- **should** — `mergedListing` re-spells `mcp.ts`'s `readMergedItems` (the same three-outcome unwrapping of `getMetaItems`); export the one and read it from both.
- **should** — the PR body's Verification "Premise" line can keep the red/green counts and drop the per-leg expected-status text, which restates the rule's inverse at finer grain than the body needs (security-findings §6).
- **should** — record the snapshot-to-dispatch window in `actionHandlerOwnerRefusal`'s header as accepted, the way `disabledActionRefusal`'s header records the in-process caller (① item 7).
- **should** — the file's `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry anchors ADR-0090 only; the gate implements ADR-0066 D4 and ADR-0126 §8 item 2 at a second site and could carry an anchor.
- note — for an object-less entry the gate reads the merged object listing on every call; the overlay cache (`meta-overlay-cache.ts`) bounds the cost, and no reading here says it is a problem.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 动作分发命中的处理器如果属于另一个已声明的动作，REST `/actions` 和 MCP `run_action` 两个入口都会同时套用那个动作的权限要求（403）和启停开关（409），与被调用动作自己的门取并集，只收窄不放宽。
- **为什么改：** 加固规则：一个处理器只有一套门，任何声明经由它运行，都要过拥有它的那个动作的门。
- **风险与回滚：** 只影响两个声明共用一个处理器的调用；仓内发运代码没有这种形态。回滚即撤本 PR。
- **需要您做的：** 无，席位经合并队列落地（非受管面，734 行）。
- **席位意见：** ACCEPT。完整达档复审 PASS（6675830049），无必改项。
